subject: Meteorology
title: The Telegraph and Weather Maps
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Telegraph and Weather Maps.

hook.text: The telegraph transformed meteorology—for the first time, weather data from distant stations arrived in real time.

buildup.text: Before the telegraph, weather data arrived by mail—by the time you got a report, the weather had already changed.

discovery.text: In 1849, the Smithsonian Institution began plotting telegraphed observations on a map—the first synoptic weather map.

twist.text: Storms could now be tracked as they moved—for the first time, warnings could outrun the weather itself.

climax.text: The telegraph made weather forecasting possible—a technology for communication became a tool for saving lives.

punchline.text: Dots and dashes on a wire—and weather maps became real-time.

quiz.question: How did the telegraph change meteorology?
options: It enabled real-time sharing of observations across distances
